_why: The two blind spots the module docstring called permanent are now classified, and these mutations ask whether the classification actually bites. The load-bearing row is `widen-terminal-line-to-admit-timeout`: that is the EASY fix a future author reaches for, it closes the blind spot in a way that manufactures a false attribution, and every test except one would still pass. Each mutation names the ONE test it is aimed at, so a kill by an unrelated assertion, a crash or a timeout is reported as a survivor with the real catcher named.

mutations.name: widen-terminal-line-to-admit-timeout
mutations._mechanism: THE fix a future author reaches for: admit the timeout name into the terminal-exception pattern and let crash_kill attribute it. It closes the blind spot and manufactures an attribution pytest cannot support — the timeout belongs to the test file that set it, not the mutated module. Must be caught by test_the_terminal_line_pattern_still_refuses_the_timeout_name, which is the only test that can see it.

mutations.name: timeout-kill-always-returns-none
mutations._mechanism: The silent pass: timeout_kills stays 0 forever and a hang is invisible exactly as before the fix. Caught by the bare-name recognition test.

mutations.name: timeout-pattern-loses-the-undotted-spelling
mutations._mechanism: `from subprocess import TimeoutExpired` prints the bare name; requiring a dotted prefix misses it. A corpus that only ever writes `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` cannot catch this, which is why the fixture does.

mutations.name: untargeted-counter-never-increments
mutations._mechanism: The blind spot restored: untargeted rows are scored and not counted, so `untargeted=0/12` prints for a spec with no `test` key anywhere.

mutations.name: untargeted-counter-increments-for-targeted-rows-too
mutations._mechanism: The opposite error, and the reason the counter needs BOTH directions tested: a counter that always fires reports every spec as fully untargeted and passes the counted-as-untargeted test.
mutations.find:
scoring_command = None
            if target_command and mutation.get("test"):

mutations.name: untargeted-loses-its-denominator
mutations._mechanism: `untargeted=3` alone is the bare count whose two causes read the same — the exact defect `crash_visible` was added to fix, reintroduced on the token this run added.

mutations.name: untargeted-branch-stops-classifying-crashes
mutations._mechanism: Restores the original gap precisely: the untargeted branch scores the kill and never asks whether the traceback names the mutated file, so crash_kills undercounts on every untargeted spec. THIS ROW SURVIVED ITS FIRST RUN and the survival was correct — it was aimed at the COUNTER test, which does not read crash_kills, so the harness reported it as caught by the wrong assertion. The discriminating test was written afterwards and this row now names it. That sequence is the row's whole value: the guard did not bite until something asserted the property it protects.

mutations.name: timeout-matching-goes-back-to-a-bare-search
mutations._mechanism:
The false positive this instrument produced against itself on its first run: an UNANCHORED pattern searched over the WHOLE output matches a timeout name inside an echoed assertion source line, so `timeout_kills` counts runs that never timed out. Same hazard `crash_reports` documents for the word `Traceback`.

THE FIRST SPELLING OF THIS ROW SURVIVED, AND IT WAS INERT RATHER THAN UNCAUGHT. It replaced `.match(line)` with `.search(raw)`, which cannot restore the defect: the anchor now lives in the PATTERN (`^`), so a search over a single line that begins `E   "subprocess...` still fails to match. A mutation that cannot express the defect is not evidence about the guard — it is the `a mutation that can never fire reads as a passing battery` row, met in the wild. Both halves must go: the anchor stripped AND the scan widened to the whole output.
